transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

Since the fan is running but the oven stays cold, while the grill works fine, this points to a fault in the specific circuit that heats the main cavity (the fan oven). The most likely cause is that the circular heating element at the back has failed and stopped producing heat. Other possibilities include burnt wiring connections at that element or a faulty switch inside the control panel that isn't sending power to it. Before we consider calling an engineer, please check this:
1. Ensure the oven is switched off and cool.
2. Look through the glass door into the back of the main oven cavity (the one with the fan).
3. Locate the large circular element surrounding the fan blade.
4. Check if it looks damaged: look for cracks, blisters, or holes in the metal tube. If you see visible damage to that element, that is probably the problem and it will need replacing by an engineer (or a confident DIYer with isolation precautions). If it looks perfectly fine visually, please let me know, as we may need to check the electrical connections.
looked thru the door n cant see owt obvious tbh. the oven's hardwired to a switch on the wall, i know where it is so i can isolate it if i need to take anything off. what shud i check next?

Thanks for checking that. We need to see if it has an internal break in the heating coil. Please isolate the power at the wall switch first. 1. Remove the rear cover plate inside the oven (usually two screws).
2. Disconnect the wires from the back of the circular fan element.
3. Use a multimeter to check for continuity across the two terminals on the element itself. If it shows no resistance (infinite/OL), the element has failed and needs replacing. If it shows normal resistance (around 20-50 ohms), the element is likely okay, and we'll need to look at the wiring connections or the switch behind the control panel.

ive isolated it n took the back panel off (4 screws not 2). dont have a multimeter so cant test it, but theres a blister/split in the coil near the bottom with a black mark on it. is that the element dead then?

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
Yes, that blister/split with a black mark suggests the element has failed. The metal sheath has broken, which stops it from heating and can be dangerous if used (risk of electric shock), so please do not use the fan oven function again until it is replaced. To find the correct replacement part for you, I need the model number. It is usually on a label or plate around the frame where the door opens (or sometimes inside the door hinge area). Please let me know what that says.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its an Indesit IFW 6330 IX, read it off the plate on the door frame. can i get the element myself n fit it?

[Heading: Likely cause: fan oven element]
Yes, that blister and split suggests the fan oven element has failed. You can buy a replacement element online or from an appliance parts retailer using your model number (Indesit IFW 6330 IX). Before you order, check the product listing carefully to ensure it matches your specific model, as manufacturers sometimes change internal components. 1. Ensure the oven is isolated at the wall switch.
2. 3. Disconnect the wires from the old element terminals and remove the fixing screws holding the element in place.
4. Fit the new element, secure it with the screws, reconnect the wires tightly, and replace the rear cover plate. If you are not confident doing this yourself, or if you find burnt wiring at the terminals when you take it off, please call an engineer to do the job safely.
[Likely component involved]
